newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZOG sees upside for shareholders.
newsitem.headline: NZOG sees upside for shareholders.

text.p: New Zealand Oil and Gas Ltd said on Monday that drilling of three exploration wells over the next 6-9 months offered significant upside for shareholders.

In its December quarter report NZOG said it was well placed to achieve its objective of funding exploration costs from production revenues as the benefits of stronger Ngatoro oil production and higher oil prices took effect.
Strong oil production from Ngatoro continued, with NZOG Group's share rising 20 percent to 44,700 barrels in the quarter against 37,200 last quarter. Daily production was averaging 1,500 barrels.
Revised reserve estimates of NZOG's Kupe project were expected by March or April.

Initial interpretation of data indicated that reserves at Toru and Kupe South-4 and 5 may be greater than previous estimates, while reserves in the central field area were likely to be confirmed, NZOG said.
Drilling in the near future will focus on offshore projects in Western Australia where three exploration and one development well were planned in the next 6-9 months.

The Bugle prospect had potential for up to 60 million barrels and the second well, targeting the Buck prospect, had potential for up to 80 million barrels, the company said. A third offshore well, Cadell, had potential for up to 30 million barrels.
Two offshore wells were drilled without success in the quarter.
NZOG said it was seeking to expand its exploration portfolio and was bidding for two exploration blocks in the North West Shelf area.

Petrol production from Tubridgi and Airlie was constant in the quarter with higher oil prices assisting Airlie's profitability. Tubridgi handled over 3,207 terajoules of gas (down from 3,749). The company's share of oil from Airlie fell to 47,300 barrels from 51,100.
